(b) Why fog computing is needed (notes p.103–106): if all data were sent straight to the cloud for processing,
• last-mile bandwidth is very limited and cannot carry the huge volume of data;
• the round-trip delay is large, so real-time response is impossible;
• the gateway's backhaul link often relies on 3G/LTE or even satellite, and is unreliable;
• the backhaul and the data centre must handle too much data, and real-time analytics on big data gets harder and harder.
Fog computing distributes data processing to places near the network edge. Local analysis reduces latency, offloads the core network of a large amount of traffic, and keeps sensitive data local. Fog nodes are geographically close to the sensors and context-aware, can form distributed edge control loops, and compress/reduce the data before uploading it.

(b) Five challenges (notes Part B p.82–83):
① Scalability: there can be millions of devices, and how the system supports them is the key issue; at the network layer, IPv6 can provide a huge number of addresses.
② Security: the more connected "things", the larger the attack surface; once a device is compromised, it can become a stepping stone for attacking other devices and systems.
③ Privacy: much of the data collected by sensors relates to specific individuals and their activities and may contain sensitive information and credentials; how to protect it and with whom to share it are key questions.
④ Big data and analytics: huge numbers of sensors produce a flood of data; large volumes of data from different sources and in different formats must be processed in time to extract useful information.
⑤ Interoperability: many protocols and architectures compete for the market and for standardisation, some proprietary and some open, so different devices/networks find it hard to work together.

(i) Figure in notes Ch2 p.39; two comparisons:
• Signal bandwidth Bs vs coherence bandwidth Bc (caused by the multipath delay spread): Bs < Bc → flat fading, the fading is correlated across the whole signal bandwidth and spectral distortion is small; Bs > Bc → frequency-selective fading, different frequencies fade differently, which causes ISI in the time domain.
• Signal bandwidth Bs vs Doppler spread BD (caused by motion): Bs ≫ BD (equivalently, symbol duration ≪ coherence time Tc ≈ 1/BD) → slow fading, the channel hardly changes within a symbol; Bs comparable to or smaller than BD → fast fading, the amplitude and phase change within a symbol.
Combining the two gives four types: flat slow, flat fast, frequency-selective slow, frequency-selective fast.
<b>(ii) 为什么是 SIMO</b>：只有一个发送符号 s（一根发射天线）:
(ii) Why it is SIMO: there is only one transmitted symbol s (one transmit antenna) but two received signals y₁, y₂ (two receive antennas), each through a different channel gain h₁, h₂ with independent noise, so it is single-input multiple-output (1 × 2).
How diversity is obtained: the same s arrives over two paths that fade independently (if the antennas are far enough apart). When h₁ is in a deep fade, h₂ is most likely not; the probability that both fade deeply at once is the product of the individual probabilities, which is much smaller. The receiver combines the two branches, e.g. MRC: z = h₁*y₁ + h₂*y₂ = (|h₁|² + |h₂|²)s + noise. The effective gain is the sum of the two branches, and the diversity order is 2.

The polled node replies with Data+CF-ACK or CF-ACK. When all nodes have been polled or the CFP time is up, the AP broadcasts CF-End (p.27). Superframe = contention-free period CFP + contention period CP, started by a DTIM beacon (p.28). The AP seizes the channel with PIFS, which is shorter than DIFS, so the CFP has higher priority and is not interrupted by the CP; priority order ACK > time-bounded packets > non-time-bounded data (p.29).
AP 在 CP 末尾用 PIFS 竞争；信道忙就要等到空闲，导致下一周期的超帧缩: At the end of the CP the AP contends with PIFS; if the channel is busy it has to wait until the channel is idle, so the superframe of the next period is shortened (p.29).

DCA 也必须满足同频复用距离约束；信道借用是 DCA 的一种形式。: DCA must also respect the co-channel reuse distance; channel borrowing is a form of DCA.

DFE 在不放大噪声的情况下消掉 ISI，比线性均衡好；但一次判错会传给下一次（: The DFE removes the ISI without amplifying the noise, so it beats linear equalisation; but one wrong decision is passed on to the next (error propagation), making the error rate a little higher than ideal.

FAMA 和 DAMA 有什么区别？DAMA-FDMA 的公共信令信道 CSC: What is the difference between FAMA and DAMA? How does the common signalling channel (CSC) of DAMA-FDMA work?
FAMA 固定分配容量，需求波动时浪费很大；DAMA 按需动态分配（p.29）。: FAMA assigns capacity in fixed amounts, which wastes a lot when demand fluctuates; DAMA assigns it dynamically on demand (p.29). DAMA-FDMA treats the subchannels in a channel as a pool; when two earth stations need full-duplex communication, a pair of subchannels is assigned dynamically. Assignment is done in a distributed way by the earth stations, using the CSC: the CSC is a repeating TDMA frame of 50 slots; the 1st is for synchronisation and the other 49 are permanently assigned to 49 stations. In its own slot a station broadcasts the numbers of the subchannels it has chosen, so the other stations no longer choose them (p.30).
FCA：固定分组、简单但不灵活；DCA：按需分配、受复用距离约束、灵活但复杂: FCA: fixed groups, simple but inflexible; DCA: assigned on demand, constrained by the reuse distance, flexible but complex
FCA：每个小区预先分到固定的一组信道，用完就阻塞，即使邻区空闲；简单，适应业务: FCA: each cell gets a fixed set of channels in advance; once they are used up, calls are blocked even if neighbouring cells have free channels; simple, but adapts poorly to traffic changes. DCA: channels are not fixed; when a call arrives, an algorithm picks one from a common pool, as long as the reuse distance is respected; flexible with low blocking, but needs centralised control and more computation.
FDD 一半上行一半下行；信道数 = 载波数 × 时隙数；S/I = Q<sup: FDD: half uplink, half downlink; channels = carriers × time slots; S/I = Q<sup>n</sup>/6, N = Q²/3, take a valid value i² + ij + j²; sectored S/I = 1/(Q<sup>−n</sup> + (Q + 0.7)<sup>−n</sup>).

FDD-TDMA 信道数、由 SIR 选簇、Erlang B、小区分裂、三扇区重: FDD-TDMA channel count, choosing the cluster size from SIR, Erlang B, cell splitting, re-choosing the cluster with three sectors (Part A combined question, 25 marks).
FDMA：按频率分，每人独占窄带信道，例 AMPS；TDMA：共用载波、按时隙轮: FDMA: divide by frequency, each user has its own narrowband channel, e.g. AMPS; TDMA: shared carrier, users take turns in time slots, e.g. GSM (200 kHz, 8 slots), IS-136; CDMA: same time, same frequency, users separated by spreading codes, e.g. IS-95, WCDMA, cdma2000.
GBR 承载和 non-GBR 承载有什么区别？默认承载属于哪种？: What is the difference between a GBR bearer and a non-GBR bearer? Which type is the default bearer?
GBR：有最低保证速率，建立时永久分配资源，适合 VoIP；资源富余时可以超过: GBR: has a guaranteed minimum bit rate, with resources allocated permanently at setup; suits VoIP. When resources are spare it may exceed the GBR, up to the limit set by the MBR. Non-GBR: no rate is guaranteed and no resources are allocated permanently; suits web browsing and FTP (p.69). The default bearer must be non-GBR; it is set up when the UE attaches to the network. A dedicated bearer can be GBR or non-GBR and is set up for a new service or new QoS requirement (p.70).

① LAN 扩展：在已有有线 LAN 的场所（厂房、交易大厅、仓库）用无线覆盖大: ① LAN extension: in sites that already have a wired LAN (factory floors, trading halls, warehouses), wireless covers the large open space; ② cross-building interconnect: point-to-point wireless links connect the LANs of nearby buildings (the devices are usually bridges/routers); ③ nomadic access: mobile internet access over a medium range such as a campus; ④ ad hoc networking: a few laptops form a peer-to-peer network directly for a temporary meeting (p.7–8).
① 上下文位置感知、低时延；② 地理上分布；③ 部署在大量 IoT 终端附近；④: ① Contextual location awareness and low latency; ② geographic distribution; ③ deployment near large numbers of IoT end devices; ④ wireless communication between fog nodes and end devices (easy to scale); ⑤ used for real-time interaction; after pre-processing, upper-layer applications only batch-process part of the data (p.109).
① 功率修正用<b>比值</b> P<sub>T</sub>′/10W；② 基站: ① The power correction uses the ratio PT′/10W; ② the base station height needs two corrections (intercept and slope), and the slope term is also multiplied by log d; ③ antenna gains are in dBd, so subtract the standard value 6 directly.
① 卫星天线和地面站天线之间的距离：频率越高、卫星越高，损耗越大；② 下行时地面: ① Distance between the satellite antenna and the earth station antenna: the higher the frequency and the higher the satellite, the larger the loss; ② on the downlink, the distance of the earth station from the satellite's "boresight" point: power is highest at the centre of the coverage area and weaker further out; ③ atmospheric attenuation: depends on oxygen, water vapour, elevation angle and frequency; the lower the elevation, the more atmosphere the signal passes through (p.21–23).
① 可扩展性（数以百万计的设备，IPv6 提供海量地址）；② 安全（攻击面扩大，: ① Scalability (millions of devices; IPv6 provides a huge address space); ② security (larger attack surface; a compromised device can become a stepping stone); ③ privacy (sensor data is tied to personal activity); ④ big data and analytics (huge, multi-source, multi-format data must be processed in time); ⑤ interoperability (many protocols and architectures, some proprietary, some open) (p.82–83).

① 节点数量多几个数量级；② 部署密集、容易失效，拓扑变化非常频繁；③ 传感器用: ① Orders of magnitude more nodes; ② dense deployment and failure-prone nodes, so the topology changes very often; ③ sensors communicate by broadcast, whereas ad hoc networks are mainly point-to-point; ④ power, computing capacity and memory are all very limited (p.56). So ad hoc network protocols cannot simply be reused.

问题：最后一公里带宽很小；时延大，做不到实时响应；网关回程依赖 3G/LTE 甚: Problems: last-mile bandwidth is very small; latency is high, so real-time response is impossible; gateway backhaul relies on 3G/LTE or even satellite and is unreliable; the data volume on the backhaul is too large; big data keeps growing, so real-time analysis becomes almost impossible (p.105). Fog computing: distribute data management as close to the network edge as possible; any device with compute, storage and network connectivity can be a fog node. Analysing data near where it is produced cuts latency, offloads traffic from the core network and keeps sensitive data local (p.106).
问题：相对地面运动快，多普勒频移大；大气阻力大，轨道逐渐衰退；需要多个轨道面、每: Problems: fast motion relative to the ground, so large Doppler shift; high atmospheric drag, so the orbit gradually decays; many orbital planes with many satellites per plane are needed; communication between two places often needs handoffs between satellites (p.17). Advantages: for the same transmit power the signal is much stronger than from GEO; coverage is more local, which saves spectrum; suitable for handheld terminals (p.18). Little LEO: below 1 GHz, bandwidth under 5 MHz, rates up to 10 kbps, used for paging, tracking and low-rate messaging; Big LEO: above 1 GHz, up to a few Mbps, also offers voice and positioning (p.19).
